findings.detail: grazer_prairies flavour 'Rolls through the grass eating grass, offering nothing, fearing everything.' repeats 'grass' twice in six words. The lore is correct (§2.3: grazers carry no colour, never fight back, 'nothing here to take'), so this is only a tightening preference -- e.g. 'Rolls through the field eating it, offering nothing, fearing everything.'

grazer_mountains carries the same idle text as all four other grazers, verbatim: 'Grazes in the open, oblivious to everything but the ground in front of it, never watching for you.' and the same when_locked string. Nothing here contradicts §2.3 (harmless, colourless, bolts on lock, never fights back) -- the shared block is correct behaviour, just flat repetition across five records that could carry one distinguishing clause each.

alpha_prairies_yellow reuses the prey flavour word-for-word: 'All knuckles and no neck, it complains right up until it doesn't.' -- the same line as prey_yellow_pale/dusk/deep/rage. It is not a rule break (the Alpha is the champion of the colour you preyed on most, §2.5, so family echo is right), but the biome's apex reading with its own prey's throwaway gag undersells the fight. The same copy-down happens on all 25 Alpha records; a per-family Alpha line would fix it.

alpha_prairies_grey flavour 'Doesn't have a weak side, and hates that you keep looking for one.' is the prey_grey_* line verbatim. Same repetition note as alpha_prairies_yellow; no contradiction with §2.5, purely a freshness preference for the mirror-match boss.

alpha_wetlands_yellow emergence 'At the warning, the lair's den lights and the ground trembles as an audio cue rises - then, after a short grace period, the Yellow Alpha bursts out' compresses two separate beats of §2.5: the lair stirs at 90% of BOTH gates (the warning), and the grace period only starts when both gates actually fall. The text is not inventing a mechanic, just eliding the gate-fall between them; 'then, once both gates fall, after a short grace period...' would be exact.

miniboss_heat wind_up ends 'it never breaks and run, fighting to the end.' -- broken grammar ('breaks and run'). The claim itself is correct per §2.6 (a trait miniboss 'does not flee'), and its arena, a shore vent, correctly sits outside the lava fields Heat unlocks. Wording only: 'it never breaks and runs, fighting to the end.'

miniboss_coat opening 'Engaging it brings the foothills' other grazer-hunters closing in from the slopes around you.' borrows the GDD's own designation for the Coat carrier itself ('The shaggy grazer-hunter', §2.6) and hands it to the mob. Placement is correct -- foothills, below the cold line, not behind the peaks its own Coat opens (§2.6, §3.3 invariant 1) -- so this is a clarity nit; 'the foothills' other hunters' reads cleaner.

panel_yellow_lock_range 'Cross-Eyed Glare' / 'One good eye, one bad attitude, both fixed on dinner.' leans on the same 'one good eye' image as prey_blue_* ('One good eye and a better trigger'), and an eye-named panel bolted to 'back ridge, near shoulder blade' is a slightly odd read. Attachment itself is legal (§2.8: panels bolt anywhere across the cube's faces, never crowding the main-face traits), so this is preference only.

panel_blue_dash_power is named 'Jackrabbit Haunch Slab' but attaches at 'right flank' -- a haunch-named slab on the flank. No rule in §2.8 is broken (any non-main-face real estate is fair game); the name and the attach point simply do not agree.
panel_grey_dash_power flavour 'One leg, all business, zero warning.' against attach 'flank piston mount' -- flavour says leg, attach says flank. Legal placement per §2.8, mismatched imagery.

panel_grey_lock_range 'Doomsight Nub' sits beside panel_grey_dash_power 'Doom-Piston Flank' in the same three-panel grey set. 'Doom' twice out of three is in-register for Grey (the voice reference has 'Doom-Bringer') but reads as a thin word-pool at set level.

prairies pocket 'A dense hedge maze at the field's shoulder hiding a huddle of Dusk brawlers that regroup and press rather than scatter.' -- 'hedge maze' connotes a planted, tended structure in a world the GDD states has no plot and no builders ('The world: an eating ladder' -- the fiction is the food chain; nothing is built or ruined). It stops short of asserting a civilisation, so it is a nit, not invented lore; 'a dense hedge tangle' keeps the cover and the ecology. Tier content is correct: Dusk debuts in Prairies pockets (§2.4b).

wetlands deep_end 'the ground only gets soggier and stronger toward the lair' pairs a terrain adjective with a meat adjective on one axis and reads muddled. The underlying claims are right (§2.7: the mix shifts upward with distance from the entrance and the Alpha lair sits at the strong end; §2.4b: Deep debuts in Wetlands pockets, which the line correctly keeps 'hidden in the defended hollows').

beach pocket 'a territorial elite that will not be talked down' hangs its joke on negotiation, in a game that per §3 has no dialogue and no narrator at all. It is a comedic aside rather than a claim about a system, so nit only -- 'that gives up nothing' would land the same beat inside the register.

elite_red 'The Redline Ripper' -- 'Redline' is an engine-tachometer term, a touch outside the primal/crude/comedic brief (§3, Content & Tone Agent), though the voice reference does allow modern absurdity ('Gravity-Spitter', 'Moon-Stomper'). Family Red / tier Clash are correct: elites are the Clash tier that never wanders (§2.7).

elite_blue 'The Deadeye Warden' -- 'Warden' imports a custodial/institutional title into a world with no factions or offices; 'Deadeye' alone already does the Sniper-family work (§2.4). Not lore invention, just a register wobble toward high fantasy.
